pharm-cvs:cvmap.q: Nitrates relax vascular smooth muscle through:
pharm-cvs:cvmap.e: NO activates guanylyl cyclase → cGMP → myosin light chain dephosphorylation.

pharm-cvs:cvmap.q: Which class acts on the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase?
pharm-cvs:cvmap.e: Digoxin inhibits the pump → ↑ intracellular Na⁺ → ↑ Ca²⁺ via NCX.

pharm-cvs:cvmap.q: A 67-year-old woman with HFrEF is started on a new drug. Two weeks later she has a persistent dry cough, and serum K⁺ has risen from 4.4 to 5.3 mEq/L. Which mechanism best explains her cough?
pharm-cvs:cvmap.e: ACE (kininase II) inhibition raises bradykinin, causing cough and angioedema; hyperkalemia follows ↓ aldosterone. Neprilysin inhibitors are combined with ARBs, not used alone.

pharm-cvs:htn.q: First-line agent for hypertension in a patient with diabetes and albuminuria:

pharm-cvs:htn.e: Hydralazine is also used. RAAS inhibitors (ACEi, ARB, aliskiren) are teratogenic (renal dysgenesis).

pharm-cvs:htn.q: A 46-year-old man is started on hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure of 156/96 mm Hg. Six weeks later he wakes with an exquisitely painful, red, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint; serum urate is 9.8 mg/dL. How did the drug most likely precipitate this?
pharm-cvs:htn.e: Thiazides cause volume contraction and compete for tubular urate secretion, raising serum urate. Xanthine oxidase inhibition would lower urate (allopurinol).

pharm-cvs:ccb.q: Which CCB class mainly acts on vascular smooth muscle?
pharm-cvs:ccb.e: Non-dihydropyridines act more on the heart (↓ HR, ↓ AV conduction).

pharm-cvs:ccb.q: A common adverse effect of dihydropyridine CCBs:
pharm-cvs:ccb.e: Also flushing, headache, gingival hyperplasia; verapamil causes constipation.

pharm-cvs:ccb.q: A 69-year-old man with hypertension and stable angina is started on a new drug. Three weeks later he reports constipation; HR is 54/min and the ECG shows a PR interval of 0.24 s. Which drug was most likely started?
pharm-cvs:ccb.e: Verapamil (non-dihydropyridine) slows SA/AV nodal conduction and causes constipation. Dihydropyridines cause reflex tachycardia and edema rather than AV block.

pharm-cvs:vasodil.e: Also reflex tachycardia; co-give a β-blocker. Used in pregnancy.
K⁺ channel opener in arterioles; reflex tachycardia and fluid retention.

pharm-cvs:vasodil.q: A 41-year-old woman treated for months with an arteriolar vasodilator for hypertension develops arthralgias, a malar rash and pleuritic chest pain. ANA and anti-histone antibodies are positive; anti-dsDNA is negative. Which patient factor most increased her risk?
pharm-cvs:vasodil.e: Hydralazine-induced lupus is more common in slow acetylators, who keep higher drug levels. TPMT deficiency predisposes to azathioprine/6-MP toxicity, not drug-induced lupus.

pharm-cvs:htnemerg.q: Which drug is used in hypertensive emergency and can cause cyanide toxicity?
pharm-cvs:htnemerg.e: Short acting; ↑cGMP via direct NO release.
Dilates renal vessels and promotes natriuresis; useful in hypertensive emergency with renal concerns.

pharm-cvs:htnemerg.q: A 58-year-old man has sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back. BP is 210/120 mm Hg in the right arm and 170/100 mm Hg in the left, HR 108/min; CT angiography shows a type B aortic dissection. Which IV drug should be given first?
pharm-cvs:htnemerg.e: In aortic dissection, β-blockade (labetalol or esmolol) comes first to lower HR and dP/dt. Pure vasodilators given alone cause reflex tachycardia and increase shear stress.

pharm-cvs:nitrates.e: Reduced preload lowers myocardial O₂ demand.
Severe hypotension. Tolerance develops; need a nitrate-free interval.

pharm-cvs:nitrates.q: A 63-year-old man with stable angina has taken isosorbide dinitrate every 6 hours around the clock for 3 months. His angina, initially well controlled, has returned at the same dose. Which change is most appropriate?
o: Shorten the dosing to every 4 hours
pharm-cvs:nitrates.e: Continuous exposure causes nitrate tolerance; an 8–12 h nitrate-free interval restores efficacy. A 24-hour patch maintains exposure and worsens tolerance.

o: Blocking the If current in the SA node
Blocking β₁ receptors in the SA node
pharm-cvs:antianginal.e: ↓ diastolic wall tension; may prolong QT.

o: Blocking L-type Ca²⁺ channels in the AV node
Blocking β₁ receptors in the SA node
Blocking the If (funny) current in the SA node
Increasing vagal tone via M₂ receptors
pharm-cvs:antianginal.e: Used in HFrEF with HR ≥ 70 on maximal β-blocker; may cause luminous phenomena.

pharm-cvs:antianginal.q: A 66-year-old man has persistent exertional angina despite maximal metoprolol and amlodipine. Resting HR is 52/min and BP 102/64 mm Hg. A drug is added that reduces angina without lowering HR or BP. What is its mechanism?
o: Release of NO in venous smooth muscle
Inhibition of late inward Na⁺ current
Blockade of the If current in SA node
pharm-cvs:antianginal.e: Ranolazine inhibits the late Na⁺ current, reducing Ca²⁺ overload and diastolic wall tension without hemodynamic effects. Ivabradine (If block) would further lower an already slow HR.

pharm-cvs:hf.q: Which diuretic class reduces mortality in HFrEF?
Hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate is especially beneficial in:
o: Patients with HFpEF and atrial fibrillation
pharm-cvs:hf.e: Also used when ACEi/ARB/ARNI are not tolerated.

pharm-cvs:hf.q: A 63-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 30%) takes lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, furosemide and spironolactone. He develops painful bilateral breast enlargement. Which drug is the most appropriate substitute to keep the mortality benefit?
pharm-cvs:hf.e: Spironolactone's antiandrogen effect causes gynecomastia; eplerenone is a more selective MRA that also reduces HFrEF mortality. Amiloride spares K⁺ but has no proven HF mortality benefit.

pharm-cvs:digoxin.e: Low K⁺ increases digoxin binding to the pump; also renal failure and verapamil, amiodarone, quinidine.

pharm-cvs:digoxin.q: Classic ECG/vision signs of digoxin toxicity:
o: Delta waves, short PR interval, wide QRS
pharm-cvs:digoxin.e: Nausea, blurry yellow vision, AV block; worse with renal failure and hypokalemia.

pharm-cvs:digoxin.q: A 76-year-old woman with HFrEF and atrial fibrillation has a ventricular rate of 118/min and BP 92/58 mm Hg. A drug is added that increases contractility and also slows the ventricular rate. By which mechanism does it slow AV conduction?
o: ↑ Vagal tone at the AV node
K⁺ channel block in nodal tissue
β₁ blockade at the AV node
L-type Ca²⁺ block in the AV node
pharm-cvs:digoxin.e: Digoxin's parasympathomimetic (vagal) effect slows AV nodal conduction; its inotropy comes from Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase inhibition. β-blockers and CCBs would lower BP and contractility further.

pharm-cvs:statins.e: Myopathy risk rises with fibrates, niacin and CYP3A4 inhibitors.

pharm-cvs:statins.q: A 52-year-old woman with LDL 182 mg/dL is started on a drug that inhibits the rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis. Eight weeks later her LDL is 96 mg/dL. Which change chiefly accounts for the fall in plasma LDL?
pharm-cvs:statins.e: Statins lower hepatocyte cholesterol, activating SREBP-2 to upregulate LDL receptors that clear LDL. Reduced intestinal absorption is the mechanism of ezetimibe.

pharm-cvs:nonstatin.e: Blocks cholesterol absorption at the brush border → lowers LDL; well tolerated.
Also impair absorption of other drugs and fat-soluble vitamins; GI upset.

pharm-cvs:nonstatin.q: A 42-year-old man with familial hypercholesterolemia has tendon xanthomas and LDL 190 mg/dL despite maximal atorvastatin plus ezetimibe. He starts a subcutaneous monoclonal antibody every 2 weeks. What is its mechanism?
o: Inhibits MTP to block VLDL assembly
pharm-cvs:nonstatin.e: PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab, alirocumab) stop PCSK9 from targeting LDL receptors for lysosomal degradation. NPC1L1 is ezetimibe's target, already on board.

pharm-cvs:tg.e: Best for lowering TG; risk of gallstones and myopathy with statins.
Prostaglandin-mediated; niacin can also cause hyperglycemia and hyperuricemia.

pharm-cvs:tg.q: A 47-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes was admitted last month for acute pancreatitis. Fasting triglycerides are 1,150 mg/dL; LDL is 110 mg/dL. Which drug is most appropriate to lower his risk of recurrence?
pharm-cvs:tg.e: Fibrates (PPAR-α → ↑ lipoprotein lipase) are the most effective TG-lowering drugs. Bile acid resins such as colesevelam can raise triglycerides.

pharm-cvs:class1.q: Which class I agent is used for ventricular arrhythmias after MI?
Class IC drugs are contraindicated in:

A 64-year-old man is treated with a class IA antiarrhythmic for atrial fibrillation. Two weeks later he has tinnitus, headache, blurred vision and diarrhea, and his QTc has lengthened. Which drug is he most likely taking?
pharm-cvs:class1.e: Cinchonism (tinnitus, headache, visual and GI upset) is characteristic of quinidine. Procainamide is also class IA but is known for drug-induced lupus, not cinchonism.

pharm-cvs:class2.q: β-blockers slow conduction mainly at the:
pharm-cvs:class2.e: ↓ Phase 4 slope and ↑ PR interval in nodal tissue. Esmolol is very short acting; metoprolol is used for rate control.
Nonselective agents worsen bronchospasm; may mask hypoglycemia.

pharm-cvs:class2.q: A 60-year-old man with type 1 diabetes starts propranolol after a myocardial infarction. A week later he is found confused with capillary glucose 42 mg/dL and says he never felt shaky or had palpitations. Why were his warning symptoms absent?
pharm-cvs:class2.e: β-blockers mask adrenergic hypoglycemia symptoms (tremor, palpitations) and nonselective agents also blunt glycogenolysis. They do not stimulate insulin secretion.

pharm-cvs:class3.e: Also hepatotoxicity. Check PFTs, LFTs and TFTs; blue-gray skin and corneal deposits.

pharm-cvs:class3.q: Class III agents prolong the action potential by blocking:
pharm-cvs:class3.e: Prolong QT; sotalol and dofetilide carry torsades risk.

pharm-cvs:class3.q: A 68-year-old man on long-term antiarrhythmic therapy has 3 months of dry cough and dyspnea with bibasal crackles; CT shows reticular opacities and DLCO is reduced. He also has blue-gray facial skin and TSH 11 mU/L. Which drug is most likely responsible?
pharm-cvs:class3.e: Amiodarone causes pulmonary fibrosis, thyroid dysfunction (iodine content) and blue-gray skin. Sotalol and dofetilide mainly cause QT prolongation/torsades.

pharm-cvs:class4.q: Adenosine is the drug of choice to terminate:
pharm-cvs:class4.e: Very short acting; causes flushing, chest pain; effect blocked by theophylline/caffeine.

pharm-cvs:class4.q: A 27-year-old woman has palpitations; HR is 186/min with a regular narrow-QRS tachycardia and BP 118/74 mm Hg. Vagal maneuvers fail. A rapid IV bolus causes brief flushing and chest tightness, then sinus rhythm returns. What is this drug's mechanism?
o: A₁ receptor → K⁺ efflux at AV node
Block of K⁺ channels → long ERP
Block of L-type Ca²⁺ at AV node
Block of β₁ receptors at AV node
pharm-cvs:class4.e: Adenosine acts on A₁ (Gi) receptors, ↑ K⁺ efflux and ↓ Ca²⁺ current, transiently blocking the AV node. Verapamil blocks L-type Ca²⁺ channels and acts more slowly.

o: Reduce HF admissions and CV death
pharm-cvs:hfrx.e: Benefit is seen with or without diabetes. Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are one of the four pillars.

pharm-cvs:hfrx.q: Before starting an ARNI in a patient on an ACE inhibitor, stop the ACEi for:

A 59-year-old woman without diabetes has HFrEF (EF 32%) on sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol and spironolactone. A fourth drug is added; two months later she develops vulvovaginal candidiasis. What is the added drug's mechanism?
o: Blocks the If current in the SA node
pharm-cvs:hfrx.e: SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) cause glucosuria, predisposing to genital mycotic infections, and reduce HF death/admission even without diabetes. Neprilysin is already inhibited by sacubitril.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: เหนื่อยหอบขาบวม
title.en: Boss case: Breathless with swollen legs

boss.case: A 64-year-old man with prior MI has 3 months of exertional dyspnea, orthopnea and ankle edema. BP 128/78 mm Hg, HR 92, bibasal crackles, JVP raised. Echocardiogram: LVEF 30%. eGFR 60, K⁺ 4.3.

qs.q: Drug that relieves his congestion fastest:
qs.e: Loops relieve symptoms but do not improve survival.

qs.q: Which combination forms the core mortality-reducing therapy for HFrEF?
qs.e: The four pillars of guideline-directed medical therapy: ARNI (or ACEi/ARB), an evidence-based β-blocker, an MRA and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
Combined with valsartan; never with an ACE inhibitor (angioedema).

qs.q: Which β-blocker is NOT proven for HFrEF?
qs.e: Only carvedilol, metoprolol succinate and bisoprolol reduce mortality.

qs.q: A key lab to monitor after starting spironolactone:
qs.e: Hyperkalemia risk, especially with ACEi/ARNI and CKD.

qs.q: If he remains symptomatic in sinus rhythm with EF ≤ 35%, digoxin can:
o: Reverse LV remodeling and improve survival
Replace the need for loop diuretics
qs.e: Digoxin improves symptoms and reduces admissions only.

stem.th: หญิง 74 ปี ความดันสูงและเบาหวาน ใจสั่นมา 2 วัน ชีพจร 130 ไม่สม่ำเสมอ ความดัน 128/80
stem.en: A 74-year-old woman with hypertension and diabetes has 2 days of palpitations; pulse 130 irregular, BP 128/80.

steps.q: Drug for rate control in a stable patient with normal EF:
o: Adenosine as a repeated IV bolus
steps.e: β-blockers and non-DHP CCBs slow AV nodal conduction.

steps.q: Diltiazem slows AV conduction by blocking:

steps.e: DOACs are preferred over warfarin in non-valvular AF.

info.th: ต่อมามีหัวใจล้มเหลว ใช้ amiodarone คุมจังหวะ
info.en: She later needs amiodarone for rhythm control
